PullRequest.Title: Avoid generated titles for persistent tool groups
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Use stable `Finished with N steps` summaries for persistent tool-call groups without invoking title generation.
- Continue generating titles for thinking sections, with `Finished thinking` as the fallback when generation is disabled or fails.
- Add regression coverage for title generation, restored titles, visible step counts, and thinking fallbacks.

## Testing

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only --force` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatThinkingContentPart.test.ts` — passed (143 tests)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatThinkingContentPart.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatThinkingContentPart.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each newly finalized persistent tool group launched asynchronous utility-model title generation, including a network-backed sendChatRequest with a five-second cancellation timeout. Responses containing several alternating tool/reasoning groups could launch one request per finalized tool group without a shared concurrency limiter, consuming network/model capacity for titles that this change replaces with deterministic step counts.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Redundant utility-model network traffic and background model work scaled with the number of persistent tool groups in an agent response, with requests able to overlap while later groups continued streaming.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Persistent tool chains now set their stable step-count fallback and return before title reuse/cache/model generation, eliminating utility-model selection and chat requests for those groups while leaving title generation enabled for persistent reasoning sections.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the PR, finalizeTitleIfDefault set a fallback for isToolChain but then continued into generateTitleViaLLM. With the setting defaulting to true, a live persistent tool group without reusable metadata/cache selected copilot-utility-small and called sendChatRequest; finalizeThinkingPart is reached each time streaming transitions from one persistent group to the next and at response completion. The added early return at line 1615 now prevents that boundary, and the new test proves modelSelections remains 0 for a two-tool chain.

Scenarios.Scenario: A live agent response completes one or more compact persistent tool-call groups.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Group finalization synchronously computes and renders the deterministic step-count title. Before the diff, utility-model title generation was launched without awaiting it, so it was off the immediate UI critical path but consumed background network/model capacity; the diff returns before that work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Select copilot-utility-small and send a chat request to generate a group title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one request for each newly finalized live persistent tool group when title generation was enabled and no generated title was already attached; several alternating groups in one response could therefore issue several requests. After the diff, zero for tool groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tool-chain branch set the fallback but fell through to generateTitleViaLLM; the added return removes model selection and request generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is fire-and-forget from finalization and does not block completion rendering, but can remain active for up to the five-second cancellation timeout and consume network/model throughput while later response content streams.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct persistent tool groups finalized during an agent response after grouping; tools within one group share one title request, so multiplicity is per group rather than per tool.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Before the fix, generateTitleViaLLM had a per-call cancellation source but no shared limiter or coalescing, so requests from separately finalized groups could overlap. After the diff, tool groups launch none.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live groups can reuse generatedTitle metadata if present, but normally do not use the persisted cache because their invocations are not all serialized. The diff bypasses metadata/cache/model title paths for every tool group and uses a deterministic count in both cold and warm cases.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default-enabled configuration, fall-through into sendChatRequest, lifecycle callers, five-second timeout, and zero-selection regression test establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual group counts and utility-model request cost vary by agent response and service conditions, but the removed per-group network boundary and possible overlap are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This scenario is a concrete performance fix, recorded separately with report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: A persistent reasoning section completes with title generation enabled, disabled, unavailable, or cached.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fallback label update is synchronous. When generation is enabled and no reusable title exists, model generation remains asynchronous and off the immediate completion-render critical path; this behavior is unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Select a utility model and, when available, request a generated reasoning summary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one launched generation per uncached finalized reasoning group invocation; reusable content metadata or a warm non-local-session cache avoids it. The diff does not increase this count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reasoning groups followed the same generation, reuse, and cache path before the diff; only the fallback text for disabled/failed generation changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background generation may later replace the title but is not awaited by finalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or write the bounded generated-title profile cache for non-local serialized sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache lookup for an eligible serialized reasoning group and one write after successful generation; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache eligibility and lookup/write behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cache lookup occurs synchronously during finalization, but the diff neither adds it nor increases its cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of uncached reasoning groups, after generated-title metadata and persisted-cache hits are accounted for.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each reasoning group can have one asynchronous generation call; no new concurrency or limiter change is introduced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm generatedTitle metadata or a valid persisted non-local cache entry bypasses model work; expired/missing entries generate once. Disabled generation and model-selection failure now use 'Finished thinking' rather than a step count, without changing cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed fallback selection is constant-time and all expensive boundaries remain on unchanged lines and paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model availability and latency vary, but there is no diff-caused increase in requests, storage work, or retained data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the changed fallback string does not alter expensive work or scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: A completed or restored persistent tool group is collapsed, expanded, or has tool-row visibility change.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion and visibility changes update the title and expansion state synchronously. Lazy tool DOM is materialized only on first expansion; the diff preserves that behavior and now always uses the inexpensive visible-step count for the title.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible tools in the already-grouped chain; counting uses appendedItemCount minus the hidden-ID set size, so title refresh is constant-time rather than scanning rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached after the new tool-chain early return; visibility observers run synchronously per changed tool visibility.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Restored generated titles and persisted title-cache values are deliberately ignored for tool groups; this does not cause misses to trigger generation because the early return also bypasses generation entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tests establish zero materialization before expansion and deterministic count updates after visibility changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM update cost depends on UI state, but the changed title calculation is constant-time and lazy materialization remains bounded to first expansion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the change avoids title model work without adding eager DOM construction or collection scans.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. The PR removes a default-enabled, per-persistent-tool-group utility-model request with unbounded cross-group overlap; that shipped regression fix was recorded against its blamed introducing commit.
